target_customer: Mexican e-commerce merchants and retailers that ship parcels and want one place to compare carriers, buy labels and track orders
problem: Small and mid-size sellers in Mexico had to deal with many carriers separately, with no easy way to compare rates, print labels, track packages and handle returns.
business_model: B2B SaaS and shipping aggregator: margin on carrier rates plus plans by shipment volume, later fulfillment and insurance-style protection

founders.name: Tavo Zambrano
previous_startups: Online ordering platform sold to Delivery Hero in 2014 (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page also lists a 500 Startups MV Batch 6 stint. LatAm List (2018) names him Jose Zambrano.

founders.name: Armando Solbes
founders.background_notes: YC page: consultant, financial strategist and advisor to startups.

founders.name: Oscar Victorin
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in the 2021 TechCrunch article; no role given.

founders.name: Daniel Alvarado
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in the 2021 TechCrunch article; no role given.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs integrations with many carrier APIs and e-commerce stores plus label and tracking workflows, standard engineering with messy carrier integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Carrier aggregation is replicable by rivals, but store integrations and negotiated carrier rates build some stickiness.

incumbents: Carriers such as DHL, FedEx, Estafeta
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent carrier is reported to have copied or bought it; the company itself bought Brazilian Frenet in December 2024 per CB Insights via LatAm List.

market_need_then: Mexican e-commerce was growing and sellers faced fragmented carriers; the 2018 LatAm List article cites the founders aiming for Amazon-level logistics for Latin American businesses.

branding.domain_note: Operates on skydropx.com (YC lists http://skydropx.com); acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Spanish, practical, aimed at small sellers per the homepage

brand_strength.rationale: Searches found no press about the brand itself; early coverage used the name Skydrop, and the name overlaps with unrelated drone brands.

outcome_analysis: Skydropx rode the growth of Mexican e-commerce, raised about 4.5 million dollars after YC in 2018 and a 20 million dollar Series A in October 2021, and expanded across Latin America, ending as an active company with a reported team of about 320 and a December 2024 acquisition of Brazil's Frenet. Defensibility rests on integrations and carrier relationships rather than deep technology.
notes: TechCrunch 2021 says the Series A adds to an earlier 7 million raised after YC; LatAm List (2018) gives 4.5 million with 6.5 million total, so the gap is unresolved. Aggregators list a Series B in August 2022 with undisclosed amount, unverified and not recorded. Total raised about 26 to 27 million per aggregators. Competitors: no 2018 dated source naming Mexican shipping-aggregator rivals was found (a 2019 Contxto piece names none), so the list is empty. Founding year conflicts (2014 per TechCrunch, 2015 per YC page, 2017 elsewhere). Funding fields from LatAm List, TechCrunch.
